_meta.note: Industry, peers, street (notes standing on 30-Sep-2026), ownership (Jun-2026), moat, critiques, gaps and conflicts for the Granules India initiation.

industry.usGenerics: The US buys ~72-75% of Granules' output. US generics are a volume business where prices fall every year once several makers are approved; shortages reward reliable suppliers. Wholesalers are consolidating purchases with fewer, dependable vendors (GPI President, 29-Sep-2026).
industry.controlled: Schedule II drugs (ADHD stimulants, opioids) are regulated by the DEA as well as the FDA: each maker gets a yearly quota and both API and dosage must be made in the US. Quota cuts caused ADHD shortages after 2023. US ADHD market ~USD10.7 bn and controlled-substance market ~USD55 bn in CY25 (Elara, citing company and Grand View Research).
industry.api: Commodity APIs (paracetamol, metformin, ibuprofen) are dominated by Chinese and Indian makers; prices spiked after COVID and then fell. Granules' API revenue fell 54% from FY23 to FY25 (Rs1,341 cr to Rs619 cr). Chinese competitors cut DCDA prices sharply in 2025-26 (CMD).
industry.peptides: Demand for peptide manufacturing capacity is rising with GLP-1 (diabetes and obesity) drugs; liquid-phase synthesis is gaining as peptides scale from kilograms to tonnes. India's peptide CDMOs are small; Senn had ~USD20 mn of revenue in FY26.

moatVerdict: Narrow moat at best, and only in US controlled substances. The rest is a well-run, cost-focused generics business without pricing power.
critiques: Gagillapur has been under OAI/warning letter for two years; 9 approvals (~USD11 bn market) are blocked and the re-inspection date is the FDA's call. A second failure would push launches out by another 12-18 months.
More than half of revenue is still legacy molecules (56% legacy generics in FY26) sold on price; costs rose in 2026 and Granules held back supply rather than pass them on.
The US is ~72-75% of revenue; US generic prices fall every year once competition arrives.
Working capital is heavy (29-33% of sales; inventory Rs1,673 cr); FY26 operating cash flow was 67% of EBITDA.
Governance: CMD pay Rs28.4 cr (4.8% of profit), four family executive directors, cheap promoter warrants.
The peptide CDMO is small and loss-making; the USD50 mn target is three years away and depends on customers' clinical programmes.
The stock re-rated from ~15-18x one-year-forward EPS (dates in FY22-FY24) to ~23x Sep-28E and ~25x FY28E on the 'Granules 2.0' story; it was ~19x during FY26 before the Q4/Q1 beats.
